players.product: US utility - transformer buyer (HICO America customer)

quarterly_data.signal: First quarter operating earnings were $0.95 per share ($0.69 per share GAAP); management affirmed all financial guidance from the fourth quarter call and continues to guide to annual earnings growth at the midpoint of its 5%-7% range, with a bias starting in 2028 toward the upper half of the range; it is monitoring catalysts that could enhance and/or extend the long-term growth rate (battery storage, Millstone, other regulated capital).
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 operating EPS $0.95 per share; GAAP $0.69 per share; 5%-7% long-term EPS growth range

quarterly_data.signal: Over 50 GW of data center capacity in various stages of contracting, including approximately 10.4 GW contracted under electric service agreements; management sees 'accelerating and durable demand' from data center customers, added commitments in all stages of contracting since December, and reports 'no detectable change' in demand despite PJM capacity-pricing and cost-allocation uncertainty. Commission-approved large load provisions make data center customers fund the infrastructure for their growth.
quarterly_data.figure: over 50 GW data center capacity in contracting stages; approximately 10.4 GW under electric service agreements

quarterly_data.signal: New Virginia law (House Bill 895 / Senate Bill 448) requires Dominion to petition for 20 GW of short- and long-term storage projects by 2045, up from the prior requirement of 3 GW by 2035. The $65 billion five-year capital plan already includes about $2 billion or about 3% for battery storage; management's rule of thumb is $2.5 billion-$3 billion per gigawatt installed (including transmission and network upgrades), expects 'some upward bias' to the 5-year capital plan and a higher run rate in the 2030s, with the update coming in the fall IRP and the Q4 capital plan; pilots on longer-duration storage are underway.
quarterly_data.figure: 20 GW storage by 2045 (vs 3 GW by 2035); about $2 billion or about 3% of the $65 billion plan for battery storage; $2.5 billion-$3 billion per gigawatt

quarterly_data.signal: Capital plan trajectory: the most recent five-year plan update was an increase of 30% of capital, and the one before that was about 15% higher than the prior; management continues to see opportunities to deploy regulated capital across generation, transmission and distribution to meet demand growth. Year to date ~$1.2 billion of ATM equity issued, leaving $400 million-$600 million for the rest of the year; FFO to debt above 15%.
quarterly_data.figure: increase of 30% of capital in latest five-year plan; prior update about 15% higher; approximately $1.2 billion ATM equity YTD; $400 million-$600 million remaining

quarterly_data.signal: Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind is over 75% complete with first power delivered in March; all 176 transition pieces and all three substations installed; nine turbines completed, with the last four averaging approximately two days per installation. Majority of turbines expected in service by the end of 2026, remainder in early 2027 prior to the end of June. Budget now $11.4 billion (approximately $100 million lower on tariff assumption changes), unused contingency $123 million; each additional quarter beyond July 2027 would add between $150 million and $200 million; potential Section 232 steel tariff impact in the $200-ish million range, possibly offset by PJM network-upgrade cost reallocation. Expected customer fuel savings of approximately $5 billion over the first 10 years.
quarterly_data.figure: over 75% complete; nine turbines completed; budget $11.4 billion; unused contingency $123 million; between $150 million and $200 million per additional quarter beyond July 2027; Section 232 $200-ish million range

quarterly_data.signal: Millstone nuclear recontracting: the facility bid into Connecticut DEEP's zero carbon energy RFP in March (decisions expected in the second quarter, negotiations with utilities in the third quarter, then up to 180 days of PURA review). It is currently contracted a little more than half through August of 2029; management would be willing to contract more than the 55%, other New England states have expressed interest, and there is continued interest from data centers to contract at Millstone (any outcome must have Connecticut stakeholder support).
quarterly_data.figure: contracted a little more than half through August of 2029; willing to contract more than the 55%

quarterly_data.signal: Asked about joining a utility consortium to build new AP1000s backed by hyperscaler off-takers, management said Dominion holds an early site permit at North Anna and has been exploring SMRs, but any nuclear structure must address first-of-a-kind risk and cost overrun risk and protect the balance sheet; it will continue to explore alternatives on that basis.
